This method of redeeming a Norton subscription via a “Product Key”, is not available on Apple devices… according to policies Apple placed, which Norton claims.

If the latter is true, Apple needs to change their policy, as this is a privacy violation!

The invitation link, allows family members or roommates to have access to your Bitdefender subscription and all its features, via their own account setup and credentials.

reviews.title: VPN issues + Random Renewal Notification
reviews.text:
I'm still trying to wrap my head around the issue. 

I checked my other devices, and there was no issue. The wi-fi was stable, laptop and gaming consoles had no issue, ONLY my iPhone while connected to the VPN.

This isn't the first time this happened. The first time it happened, I reset my entire wi-fi/connection settings, and everything worked fine. The drawback was that my VPN (SearchWeb) wouldn't connect on demand if I went without wifi. I had to manually turn it on every time. 

Two days ago, I noticed that my Wi-Fi wasn't working despite having full bars. I couldn't send videos, check the internet or use social media. The "No Internet Connection." logo popped up while connected to the Wi-Fi. My VPN was connected, safe search and everything else was on. The moment I turned off the VPN, everything started working again. No "offline mode" or "no internet connection", it was fine.

Around last month, I received a notification claiming my subscription expired, and I had to renew it. Panicked, I checked the app and there was no issue. Checking the App Store, the subscription was still active for another year. I never cancelled it, so I was confused.

After two years of perfect service, I'm confused on why nothing is working all of the sudden.

reviews.title: Serious Flaw Needs Urgent Attention
reviews.text: On iOS, every heading in Norton 360 shows “tabbar-home-title,” which appears to be an internal developer label mistakenly exposed to users. This is a basic UI failure and completely unacceptable in a paid security product. It undermines confidence in the app’s quality and raises concerns about overall reliability. This needs to be fixed urgently. I note this has already been reported by another user but no action taken. If Norton is incapable of writing basic code how can it be trusted with customers data and device security ?

reviews.title: Not worth auto renewing
reviews.text:
Auto renew each year is a complete rip off @ £89.99!
If you decide to use Norton 360 beware of the auto renewal and ensure to cancel each year! Go to amazon, curry’s or any other retailer to pick up subscription at a fraction of the cost. Be sure to check around as you can get a new copy of Norton 360 deluxe for as little as £10!
Once you cancel the auto renewal they then offer to renew your service for £29.99 vastly lower than the auto renewal cost but still cheaper to buy a new years subscription from another retailer at a much better price than they offer. They claim to give you extra services when you automatically renew but I have never noticed any difference for the costly renewal. Don’t be a fool like I have for the past few years  by renewing and save your hard earned cash for a cheap new subscription from curry’s (which is the cheapest place I found for a years subscription).
Wouldn’t recommend Norton to anyone and will be looking for an alternative virus protection provider once my Norton subscription ends.
To add insult to injury a recent update to app has bugs that stop it from operating correctly. The instructions to fix the problem like restarting phone or reinstalling app don’t work either. As an iPhone user you don’t have access to clear cache like you do from an android operating system.

reviews.title: Far Worse VPN Protection Than Norton VPN
reviews.text:
For the past few months, I’ve been struggling with forced, prolonged disconnects using Norton 360’s VPN. I have had to go to Settings > VPN on my iPhone 14 to turn it on when the Connect button within 360 doesn’t work. And to change countries, I’ve had to close 360, restart my phone and then reopen 360 to have control of that Connect button and to be able to choose countries. Meanwhile, Proton VPN doesn’t have that issue if I choose it. Additionally, 360 doesn’t have a kill switch option. So 360 will disconnect constantly and I’ll be unprotected the whole time. I’ve been waiting for an update to fix this. So far, I haven’t seen one from January - March 2026.

Looking up options for Norton VPN becauseI wanted to configure ipsec, I saw directions on Norton’s site for changing the settings from ipsec to other protection/masking protocols, and for enabling deeper forms of protection. On a hunch, I found Norton VPN on the App Store and installed it. Instantly, the extra protection and flexibility I needed were there and so was the kill switch! I went from hours every day trying to get a strong, protected signal to having a version of Norton VPN that worked.

None of 360’s features - supposed dark web protection (really dark web reporting that does nothing else), web browsing protection that only works if the 360 VPN is enabled until *it* doesn’t work — none of it matters if you can’t rely on the VPN. 

So until 360 has anything like the multiplicity of Norton VPN, I advise you to

reviews.title: Lots of issues
reviews.text:
I have been a Norton customer for some time, but my experience recently has been extremely frustrating.

Tonight was the final straw. I received repeated warnings flagging legitimate apps as suspicious, despite downloading them directly from the official App Store and having fully up-to-date software. The alerts disappear, then reappear again, which makes it impossible to know whether there is a genuine issue or just another false alarm.

I am also constantly being logged out of safe emails, almost every other day and never easy to get connected. 
The system does not seem to recognise that I am the same user across platforms, and the app, website and email communications do not appear to “speak” to each other properly. It creates confusion rather than reassurance.

The Protection Report is another concern. It provides impressive-looking figures about blocked threats, but gives no meaningful detail. What were these threats? Were they malicious websites? Security device issues? Suspicious connections? There is no clear explanation, so the numbers feel like statistics without substance.

Security software should provide clarity and confidence. Instead, I am left feeling uncertain and repeatedly having to troubleshoot problems that may not even exist.

At the moment, the experience feels more stressful than protective.

reviews.title: VPN issues
reviews.text: Have had a subscription for a few years now but for the last three months I’ve been having issues where the VPN is effectively blocking any emails coming through. When I toggle it on and off this results in ‘bunched’ emails coming through - sometimes a trickle sometimes two days worth of emails at a time. It’s causing really issues with personal and professional emails and is not reflecting well on me with family, friends, colleagues or clients. Not sure I’ll be renewing this year when it’s due to expire

reviews.title: Revised access and layout
reviews.text: Where is the simple efficient dashboard ?? Update is overly wordy and difficult to navigate - ChatGPT had to advise route through menus etc after I saxo only a ‘subscription confirmation’ page and ‘account management’ - NOT user friendly but I imagine dozens of smart ‘techies’ think that this is a technological advancement !!

reviews.title: Sort of works….BUT GIVE ME YOUR MONEY, GIVE ME MORE MONEY
reviews.text:
It may be an adequate defence, but they seem to prioritise monetization over everything else. Complex setup, in which bits work, then don’t. A lack of ability to recognise that you can have two iPads as part of your ten devices means I’m constantly getting OTPS. Once it’s set up, it’s fine, but it’s constantly gatekeeping your subscription and dear god, is that subscription expensive. £149 for a year. Add in the constant nagging to add driver scanner, pc clean up and fake alarms designed to gull you into upgrades that you don’t need and will probably never use.

This is my last year with Norton. The competition has got to be better than this. I want something that will work quietly, unobtrusively and effectively in the background . I don’t want reports boasting of achievements of little merit, promotional scareware and constant logging in. And don’t get me started on password manager not being able to point to an app to use if you create an account on a website.

I need to calm down, but this is an ecosystem you don’t want to get involved with. I have and its broken me,
